title: Connector manifest
description: What a connector is and does (PRD-001 FR-INT-25, FR-INT-26, FR-INT-27): the services it implements, what it needs, what it sends out and where, and what pause and disable do to its work. Every first-party connector in connectors/<id>/manifest.json validates against it; third-party connectors (FR-INT-28, P3) will use the same format.

id.description: Stable identifier; the directory under connectors/.

name.description: The provider's own name, as people know it.

version.description: The connector's version; a change to what it declares changes it.

min_platform.description: The oldest platform version it runs on.

summary.description: One plain sentence for the catalogue.

scope.description: Installed installation-wide by the Super admin, or per organisation by its Owner or Administrator.

configuration.description: A JSON Schema (2020-12) of the connector's non-secret configuration: an object whose properties are what a person sets. Secrets are never in it; they are listed under secrets.

used_by.description: The services that read it, and only they may.

rotation_overlap_hours.description: How long the replaced version stays valid after a rotation, so work in flight and webhooks signed with it still pass (FR-INT-26: rotation without downtime).

provider_scopes.description: The scopes it asks of the provider.

data_classes.description: The data classes it sends out of Fyniq (PRD-001 AI-75's classes).

regions.description: Where the provider processes what it is sent: ISO 3166 country codes, EU, or configured where the person's own server decides.

host.description: A host it may reach; *. allows its subdomains.

configured.description: The configuration property that names the host, for a server the person chooses (SMTP); reached only through the egress guard (SEC-36).

destinations.description: Every place it connects to (SEC-36); nothing else is reachable.

registered_by.description: connector: it registers and removes them itself; operator: a person sets them in the provider's dashboard, and uninstall lists them to remove.

secret.description: The secret that signs them, one of secrets.

health_check.description: What the health check does, in plain words.

test_action.description: What the connection test does; it answers pass or fail with a reason, never the provider's body.

local_substitute.description: What stands in for the provider in local mode and in tests (ADR-T4).

breaker_failures.description: Consecutive transport failures that open the circuit breaker.

breaker_cooldown_seconds.description: How long the breaker stays open before one trial.

trigger.description: Who may make it act (FR-INT-27): a completed human authority, a system rule, or nobody.

trigger_rule.description: The authority or rule, in plain words.

on_disable.description: What disable does to queued work: cancel what is safe to cancel, hold what a person asked for.

in_flight.description: Work already handed to the provider finishes, or is reconciled with it; never dropped.

parser_version.description: For a capability that reads what it imports: the parser that read each item, recorded on the item.
